title: Rollout Error-Cost Heatmap Coupler: consolidated view for canaries and cost-aware rollbacks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, actionable console widget that couples rollout state (canary/primary splits), request error taxonomy, and per-route cost heatmaps to help SREs and PMs spot cost regressions introduced by new model rollouts and trigger cost-aware rollbacks or mitigations.
background: Teams currently look at rollouts, error rates, and cost dashboards in separate surfaces. During several incidents, a canary rollout increased token spend due to repeated retries and a model producing malformed outputs, but the signal was delayed because cost and error surfaces are siloed. This widget is intended to surface correlated signals (errors ↔ retries ↔ cost per-request) in a single glance and provide fast actions (pause canary, reduce traffic, open trace).
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to see whether a canary rollout is causing an increase in per-request CPU/GPU cost within the last 15 minutes, so I can pause the rollout before it burns budget.
As a PM, I want a ranked list of routes with highest error-cost delta between baseline and canary so I can prioritize investigation.
As an on-call engineer, I want quick links from a heatmap cell to recent failed payloads and retry traces so I can form a hypothesis and mitigate.
As a platform engineer, I want to configure thresholds that trigger an automated partial rollback when error+cost spike crosses policy.
acceptance_criteria: Widget shows a 2D heatmap: X axis time (1m buckets, configurable), Y axis routes (top 10 by traffic) with color encoding combining error rate and cost-per-request delta between canary and baseline.
Clicking a heatmap cell opens a side panel with: recent failed payload samples (up to 5), retry counts histogram, dominant error taxonomy tags, and link to the trace in the trace viewer.
Top-of-widget summary shows: current canary % traffic, aggregated error delta (canary - baseline), and cost delta (per-request token spend and GPU time estimate).
Action buttons: Pause canary, Reduce canary to X% (pre-filled thresholds), Create incident with pre-populated context linking the heatmap snapshot.
Prototype covers responsive states (desktop console, narrow list view for small widths) and accessible color palette for heat intensity.
Telemetry hooks defined: heatmap cell click, action button click, snapshot export; these map to console-analytics events.
Performance: heatmap must render for 10 routes x 90 buckets under 200ms in the console with synthetic data; backend API contract documented in PRD.
Security: payload samples scrub PII per existing scrubber rules before display.
decisions: Use combined metric for color encoding: normalized z-score of (error_delta * 2 + cost_delta) to bias toward reliability impact, agreed 2026-02-25 design sync.
Limit initial route list to top 10 by traffic with 'show more' expansion to avoid overcrowding.
Default time window 90 minutes with quick options 15m/1h/6h.
design_notes: Explored three visual encodings (stacked bars, dual-axis line overlay, combined heatmap). Chose combined heatmap for scanability when teams are triaging during on-call. Side panel will reuse existing 'payload inspector' components to ensure scrubber parity. Need to add a small color legend and numeric overlay on hover for precise values.

notes_for_engineering: Backend should provide normalized baseline metrics per-route for the last 60 minutes. API must return pre-scrubbed payload samples or a reference token to request a scrubbed payload. Telemetry event names and fields listed in attachments. Document rate limits for the heatmap cell expansion API to avoid overloading upstream tracing services.
